justifications.unit: Unit tests drive the fluent when/then paths and time travel; left uncovered are the failure branches of ShouldSucceed/ShouldFailWith/GetErrorValue and the Outbox and Saga assertion helpers (OutboxShouldContain, SagaShouldBeStarted/Completed/Failed/Compensating/TimedOut), which need a configured fixture with seeded stores and are exercised through the fixture and helper tests instead.
justifications.guard: The guard flag reaches only the argument checks and the 'fake time provider not configured' guard; every fluent assertion body needs a real fixture and belongs to the unit flag.

justifications.unit: Unit tests cover registration, fake stores and time control; left uncovered are the lambda bodies of WithSingletonService/WithScopedService/WithValidator configuration callbacks and the ClearStores branch for stores that were never resolved, which only execute when a test builds the provider with those options.
justifications.guard: Only the null/argument checks of the fluent With* methods are reachable by the guard flag; the service-building and store-clearing bodies are unit-flag code.

Identity/TestIdentity.cs.reason: Declared test seam (ADR-035): builds user identities with an authenticated principal

Identity/TestRequestContext.cs.reason: Declared test seam (ADR-035): contexts carrying a test identity

justifications.unit: Unit tests cover seeding, When/Then and time travel; left uncovered are the failure branches of ThenThrows/ThenNoException, ThenCachedResponseIs and the message-state assertions (ThenMessageWasProcessed/WasFailed/IsNew, ThenInboxHasCount/IsEmpty) that only run when an assertion fails or after a handler ran, which a test would have to force to fail on purpose.
justifications.guard: Only the constructor and argument checks (null store, null time provider, null message ids) are guard-reachable; the helper's behaviour lives in the unit flag.

justifications.unit: Unit tests cover seeding, time travel and the happy When/Then paths; left uncovered are the failure branches of ThenThrows and the ThenMessageWasProcessed/WasFailed/ThenOutboxContains assertions plus GetMessage for missing ids, which execute only when an expectation is deliberately violated.
justifications.guard: Only the constructor and argument checks are guard-reachable; seeding, assertions and the time-travel logic belong to the unit flag.

justifications.unit: Unit tests cover saga seeding, step transitions and timeout advance; left uncovered are the assertion helpers' failure branches (ThenSagaStatus, ThenSagaData, ThenSagaIsAtStep, ThenSagaHasError, ThenSagaHasCompletedAt, ThenThrows/ThenNoException) and the When/WhenAsync error capture, which run only for a violated expectation or a throwing action.
justifications.guard: The guard flag reaches only the constructor and argument checks; the saga seeding and assertion bodies (the bulk of this large helper) are unit-flag code.

justifications.unit: Unit tests cover scheduling, due/recurring seeding and time advance; left uncovered are the cron, recurring, cancelled, rescheduled and due/not-due assertion helpers' failure branches, GetScheduledMessage for missing ids and the When/WhenAsync error capture, which run only for a violated expectation or a throwing action.
justifications.guard: Only the constructor and argument checks are guard-reachable, which is a small share of this very large helper; scheduling, assertions and time travel are unit-flag code.

justifications.unit: Unit tests cover module registration, mocked modules and time control; left uncovered are the Configure and WithMockedModule/WithService callback bodies and the EnsureBuilt rebuild branch, which run only when a test builds a provider with those options.
justifications.guard: Only the null and argument checks of the fluent With* methods are guard-reachable; building the provider and running module code is unit-flag code.
